svg.text: AU Bank Insurance Distribution Platform — R0 Quote Path
customer lookup → need & suitability (C1) → consent (C2) → quote · the lawful-gate half of the journey, and the five ways it is refused
THE RULE THIS HALF OF THE JOURNEY EXISTS TO ENFORCE
C1 — no quotation without a valid, unexpired suitability result. C2 — no proposal without current consent.

Both are hard gates enforced in the owning context, not checks the UI is trusted to have done. A gate that can be skipped by calling the API directly is not a gate — FF-08 and FF-09 assert exactly that.
RM signs in; permissions resolved server-side
role · branch · hierarchy · insurer scope · certification — never from the device
look up ETB customer (CIF / mobile / PAN)
purpose recorded · narrow result set · rate limited — search abuse is a named threat
CBS stays the golden source; the platform keeps a timestamped snapshot (S-04 / S-05)
the journey now has an owner, a stage and a resumable reference
evaluate — eligibility-based, never a ranking or a recommendation
records inputs, rule-pack version, outcome, reasons and a validity window
#9 stores the reference; it never stores what suitability decided (SC-W3-6)
42 consent rules · CONSENT-PACK · wording version pinned to the record
customer confirms on their own device via OTP
the RM cannot confirm consent on the customer's behalf — attributable or invalid
withdrawal is a first-class event, not an absence of a record
R0: Term Life, Group A, one insurer · eligibility + channel + effective dates
refused with 403 unless a valid unexpired suitabilityRef is presented (C1 · FF-08)
translated to the canonical contract at the seam; no insurer format travels inward
offers → normalised to the bank's common shape
expiry captured per offer; a stale offer cannot be selected
offers ordered by disclosed customer-relevant basis only
commission and bank preference are not inputs, and no field exists to make them one (QR-07)
customer selects an offer · stage := OFFER_SELECTED
hands over to the money path — see r0-money-path.svg
Everything above is the lawful-gate half. The money path picks up here: proposal → underwriting → payment → reconciliation → issuance → SOLD (r0-money-path.svg).
REFUSALS — WHAT THE PLATFORM MUST SAY NO TO, AND WHAT THE RM SEES WHEN IT DOES
no suitabilityRef, or the reference does not resolve
403 — the quote request is not attempted at the insurer
'complete the suitability assessment first', with a link to it
FF-08 asserts the API refuses, not just the UI
a warning the RM can dismiss · an override flag · a supervisor bypass
suitability outside its validity window at quote time
403 — a stale assessment is treated as no assessment
'this assessment expired on <date>, reassess to continue'
validity window is stored on the record, not computed at read
silently re-use, extend, or round the window
consent withdrawn, or the wording version has been superseded
proposal submission is blocked and the journey states why
'consent was withdrawn on <date>' — never a generic error
FF-09 · withdrawal is an event with its own record
treat absence of a withdrawal as presence of consent
customer or channel falls outside the catalogue's eligibility
the product is not listed — not listed-and-then-refused
only products that can lawfully be sold to this customer
eligibility evaluated in #8, not filtered in the client
show it, take the input, then fail at submission
the selected offer's expiry has passed
re-quote required; the expired offer cannot be carried forward
'this quote expired — request a fresh one'
expiry is a property of the offer record
honour a lapsed premium because the journey is nearly complete
asynchronous — provider call, poll or callback
#n bounded context · S-nn / FF-nn / QR-07 as used in docs/hdl.svg
